tools/c_objects.py started tools/check.py once per check, about 12,500 times in a cold NTSC-U
carry, and about 85% of each check was reading the same tables again (the level catalogues,
config/us/map.tsv, src/levels/'s source entries, the core programs' earlier declarations).

- tools/check.py: main(argv) runs one check from an argument list, and reset() (called by
  every main()) clears what a check leaves in the module (LEVEL, US, _ADDRS, DNAS). The
  command line behaves as before.
-…

commits.author: bigbeno37

commits.headline: fix(tools): c_objects.py stops when a worker reports a changed kept table
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
With CHECK_BATCH_VERIFY=1 a worker found a check that changed a table it keeps and answered
exit status 70 with a line on standard error, but c_objects.py read only standard output's
MATCH line and stored the result as usual.

- tools/check_batch.py: the reply names the changed tables ("changed"), and Worker.run()
  kills the worker and raises KeptTableChanged instead of returning that check's answer, so
  no caller can use it by mistake.
- tools/c_objects.py: on KeptTableChanged the run stops…

commits.headline: test(tools): the worker tests run their workers in verify mode
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
WorkerTest's workers now run with CHECK_BATCH_VERIFY=1, so a check that changes a table the
worker keeps fails them in CI, without the toolchain RealChecksTest needs. With a caller that
reverses the kept level catalogue in place (check.level_function), test_a_worker_answers_as_
separate_processes and test_ntsc_u_checks_in_a_worker now fail with no UYA_* variables set;
before, only the skipped RealChecksTest caught it.

commits.headline: docs(tools): say how much memory c_objects.py's check workers take
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
Each long-lived check worker takes about 210 MB (peaks of up to 215 MB measured) for the whole
c_objects.py step, against about 58 MB for one tools/check.py process before, so the JOBS=32
that AGENTS.md, docs/build/versions.md and tools/carry_us.sh give for the carry is about 7 GB
of workers (the default 16 about 3.4 GB). Each place that gives the job count says so, and so
does c_objects.py's -j help.

commits.headline: fix(tools): the reuse key follows an include in every spelling a compiler opens
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
Under wibo SN's ee-gcc 2.95.3 and Sony's 2.9-ee driver open an #include without regard to case,
take \ as a folder separator and drop the dots at the end of each part, and so do SN's
assemblers for .include; tools/includes.py looked for the name as written only, so a source
with #include "Structs/Hero.h" or "structs\hero.h" matched while its key held only a missing
include/Structs/Hero.h, and a later edit of hero.h reused a stale MATCH.

commits.headline: fix(tools): the reuse key follows the includes of a toolchain's own headers
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
tools/includes.py left a name it found in no repository folder to the toolchain, whose files
are in the key; but a toolchain header's own includes look in -I include and -I . first, so
creating include/stddef.h (or machine/types.h at the root) would change what a compile of
<stddef.h> includes without changing its key.

  folders their compilers search: SN's lib/gcc-lib/ee/2.95.3, Sony's 2.9-ee gcc-lib…

commits.headline: fix(tools): c_objects.py stores a result only while its key is still true
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
The keys were computed once, at the start of a run, and each result stored under its key when
its check ended: a file edited after the keys and before the check was checked in its new form
and stored under the old form's key, so a revert later reused that result (a stale MATCH).

- tools/c_objects.py: Watch keeps the state (os.stat: inode, size, modification and change
  time; missing) of every file and folder the keys read, taken before they read it: src/,
  include/, the root and what is…

commits.headline: fix(tools): c_objects.py stores "left as assembly" only for a check that gave a verdict
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
A compile that failed for a reason outside its inputs (the compiler killed or out of memory, a
crash of wibo, a full disk) printed COMPILE ERROR with exit status 0; the function was stored
as left as assembly and reused until one of its inputs changed.

- tools/c_objects.py: no_verdict() decides whether a check said something about the function:
  its NAME: MATCH or NAME: N diff line; or, with status 0, a COMPILE ERROR that has a
  compiler's or assembler's message about a line of its source…

commits.headline: fix(tools): the reuse key takes every header for an include with a `..` part
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
Under wibo SN's ee-gcc, Sony's 2.9-ee driver and SN's assemblers drop `x/..` from a name without looking
whether x exists: `#include "nonexist/../structs/hero.h"` opens include/structs/hero.h. The scan stopped at
the missing folder, so the header was not in the function's key and a stored MATCH was reused after the
header changed. What a `..` opens depends on the program (the Linux compilers need the folder), so
tools/includes.py no longer follows such a name: it gives None, as for a macro, and…

commits.headline: fix(tools): c_objects.py notes a path only when its times are in the past
commits.author: bigbeno37
commits.body:
Watch decides from a path's inode, size and times whether it changed during a run. Those times have the
clock tick's grain, so a write of the same size in the tick of the first look left them as they were: on
a machine whose /tmp keeps times by the tick, tests/test_reuse.py's
test_a_change_a_change_undone_and_a_new_file_count failed ("None != .../include/a.h"). Watch.note() now
waits until a path's modification and change times are two seconds in the past (Watch.RACY_NS) and takes
its state…
